calls.reason: The packet has no analysis of the actual Shearer output. Anthropic's hallucination research looks at a different model and a different mechanism, so it cannot confirm or rule out the proposed cause.

HalluLens (April 2025) tested models on questions drawn from Wikipedia. When they answered, they were wrong roughly 27% to 45% of the time, which clearly means they do not stick reliably to Wikipedia content. The benchmark assumed, but did not verify, that the models were trained on Wikipedia.

The Gemma 3 documentation fits the point that the model has no record store. Whether LLMs have a world model is contested: the Othello study found internal representations, and there is no agreed standard for the named researchers' sense of the term.

The forecast says 'eventually' and has no deadline. Graph-based retrieval and AWS reasoning checks are narrow, single-setting improvements, and a 2026 benchmark found hybrid gains were inconsistent, so nothing decides the outcome yet.
